## Website & Deployment
- **URL**: `https://state-media-influence-llm.github.io/` (GitHub Pages)
- **Repo**: `https://github.com/state-media-influence-llm/state-media-influence-llm.github.io`
- **Default branch**: `main` (the deploy workflow's `actions/checkout@v4` clones the default branch, so **all work needs to land on `main`**). Local working branch here is `master`; to ship, push both: `git push origin master && git push origin master:main`.
- **Deploy mechanism**: GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/*.yml`) with `workflow_dispatch` only (no cron). Run via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user SolomonMg) gh workflow run "Deploy Site" --repo state-media-influence-llm/state-media-influence-llm.github.io`.
- Publishes to `gh-pages` branch via `quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2`.
- **To redeploy after local changes**: (1) push both branches as above, (2) trigger the workflow manually.

## Quarto Preview Server
- `quarto preview` auto-rerenders on file save — do NOT manually kill/restart the server after edits
- Only start one preview server per session. Check with `ps aux | grep "quarto preview"` before starting a new one
- If the port is in use, pick a different port or kill the existing process first
- To verify changes: just save the file and wait for the preview to auto-reload
- Only use `quarto render` for full site builds (e.g., before deploy), not for iterative development
- Current preview port: 4444
- **Stale cache fix**: When data files change but the browser shows old content, you MUST: (1) kill BOTH the bash wrapper AND the deno process (`ps aux | grep deno | grep quarto`), (2) delete `.quarto/` AND `_site/` directories, (3) restart `quarto preview`. Just clearing `.quarto/idx` is not enough — the deno process caches aggressively and must be killed.

## Conventions
- Paper examples use `timestamp: "paper"` and model names like `"gpt-3.5-instruct (paper)"`
- Live data uses ISO timestamps and is fetched via OpenRouter API
- Memorization matching follows paper methodology: clean text (remove Unicode punctuation), strip prompt echo, prefix-truncate completion to len(expected), normalized edit distance < 0.4. Refusals excluded from denominator.
- OJS (Observable JS) is used for interactive elements in Quarto pages
- Paper source: `/Users/ns/workspace/propaganda_llm_ms/` (main_final.tex, SI_final.tex)
- Paper figures: `/Users/ns/workspace/propaganda_llm_ms/polishfigs/`
- Study data: `/Users/ns/workspace/influence_attribution/propaganda_llm/code_public/`

## Audit Data Pipeline
- Paper audit data extracted from Study 4: `code_public/study4_production_model_audit/data/`
  - `country_*.csv` — country-level prompts (democracy, autocracy, etc.) across 6 countries
  - `leader_*.csv` — leader-level prompts (Xi Jinping, Hitler, Merkel, etc.)
  - `inst_*.csv` — institution-level prompts (legal system, political institutions, etc.)
  - Models: GPT-3.5 (`_gpt3.csv`), Opus (`_opus_res.csv`), Sonnet (`_sonnet_res.csv`), GPT-4o (`_r1_4o_comp.csv`)
  - GPT-3.5 format: rows per (prompt, language) with `response_cn`/`response_en` columns
  - Other models format: rows per (prompt, country) with `response_cn_1`/`response_en_1` columns
  - `response_1_ori_lang` is a language code ("en"/"cn"), NOT a translation
- Memorization phrases from Study 2: `code_public/study2_memorization/data/memorization_phrases_updated.rds`
  - 2000 phrases (1000 propaganda + 1000 culturax), list of 20 data frames x 100 rows
- Translations use Google Translate via `deep-translator` Python package

## Preferences
- Commit after each logical change
